'''Lubna Hamid Tawfiq Tahtamouni''' ({{langx|ar|لبنى تهتموني}}; born 24 January 1976) is a [[Jordan]]ian biologist known for her work in [[developmental biology]] and [[cancer research]]. She is the head of the Department of Biology and Biotechnology at [[Hashemite University]] in [[Zarqa]], Jordan.  She has won multiple awards for her work on [[breast cancer]], and is known as an advocate for allowing young women in the Arab world to choose a career in science. In 2016, she was named one of [[100 Women (BBC)|BBC's 100 Women]].

==Early life and education==
Tahtamouni was the third of six children and was raised in [[Irbid]] in northern Jordan, a city known for its well-educated residents.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.nafsa.org/Professional_Resources/Publications/International_Educator/Women_Making_Their_Marks/|title=Women Making Their Marks|last=Wilkie|first=Dana|date=November 2016|website=International Educator|access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref> She attended the [[University of Jordan]], earning a [[bachelor's degree]] in 1997 and a [[master's degree]] in 2000.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://staff.hu.edu.jo/CV_E.aspx?id=pytjhLqE6Ao=|title=Lubna H. T. Tahtamouni|website=Hashemite University|access-date=8 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201032255/http://staff.hu.edu.jo/CV_E.aspx?id=pytjhLqE6Ao=|archive-date=1 December 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was placed in a biology program as an undergraduate due to her high test scores.<ref name=":2" />  For her master's degree she specialized in developmental and [[reproductive biology]] under [[Hameed Al Haj]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=http://en.arabwomanmag.com/dr-lubna-tahtamouni-one-of-the-top-10-scientists-in-the-world/|title=Dr. Lubna Tahtamouni, One of The Top 10 Scientists In The World|last=Al Harithi|first=Amal|date=3 May 2015|newspaper=Arab Woman Platform|access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref> 

She did her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D]]. work in the United States at [[Colorado State University]], graduating in 2005,<ref name=":0" /> working on migration of embryonic and [[Metastasis|metastatic]] cells under [[James Bamburg]]. 

She credited her family with being supportive of her career in science and her decision to relocate to the United States.<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
Throughout Tahtamouni's undergrade and master's program at the University of Jordan, she worked as a student teaching assistant for the Department of Biology, from September 1996 to December 1999.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=LUBNA HAMID TAWFIQ TAHTAMOUNI |url=https://staff.hu.edu.jo/CV_E.aspx?id=pytjhLqE6Ao= |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=staff.hu.edu.jo}}</ref> Some of the classes she oversaw were Embryology and General Practical Biology, from 1997 to 2000.<ref name=":6" />

When she went to the University of Colorado for her Ph.D, she worked as a student teaching assistant for the Department of Biology. For 3 years she helped instruct their [[Cell biology|Cell Biology]] course.<ref name=":6" />

Tahtamouni returned to Jordan after completing her Ph.D in Cell and Developmental Biology<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lubna TAHTAMOUNI {{!}} Chair {{!}} Ph.D in Cell and Developmental Biology {{!}} Hashemite University, Zarqa {{!}} HU {{!}} Department of Biology and Biotechnology {{!}} Research profile |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Lubna-Tahtamouni |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230427230430/https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Lubna-Tahtamouni |archive-date=2023-04-27 |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=ResearchGate |language=en}}</ref>. There, she set off to help inspire young women to advance their science studies<ref name=":4">{{Cite news|url=http://www.arabamerica.com/beirut-conference-awards-arab-women-in-science/|title=Beirut Conference Awards Arab Women in Science|last=El Shabrawy|first=Nevine|date=19 October 2011|last2=Al Youm|first2=Al Masry|newspaper=Arab America|language=en-US|access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref>, out of commitment to the institutions that supported her move to the United States.<ref name=":1" /> In 2008, she was named director of a microscopy facility at Hashemite University that she had secured funding for.  She also ran proposal-writing workshops for new faculty to increase their chances of gaining funding, including from foreign sources.<ref name=":2" />  She spent summers working abroad in Australia and the United States to remain up to date with current research methods.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

In 2011, she was named head of the Hashemite University Department of Biology and Biotechnology.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/worldwide-acclaim-for-ground-breaking-local-heroines/418339.article|title=Worldwide acclaim for ground breaking local heroines|last=Reisz|first=Matthew|date=8 December 2011|newspaper=Times Higher Education|access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref>  Also in 2011, she won a [[L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards|L'Oreal-UNESCO Pan-Arab Regional Fellowship for Women in Science]],<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://en.ammonnews.net/article.aspx?articleNO=14122|title=Jordanian awarded Fellowship by L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Program|date=13 October 2011|website=Ammon News|access-date=10 December 2016}}</ref> and an [[Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World|OWSD]] Award for Young Women Scientists from the Developing World,<ref name=":3" /> for her work on breast cancer, which accounts for 35% of all cancer deaths in Jordan.<ref name=":4" />  In 2015, she was named to the [[Jordan–United States relations|United States Embassy in Jordan]]'s Women in Science Hall of Fame,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://jo.usembassy.gov/women-in-science-hall-of-fame-2015/|title=Women in Science Hall of Fame – 2015|date=12 January 2015|newspaper=U.S. Embassy in Jordan|language=en-US|access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref> and she was named one of [[100 Women (BBC)|BBC's 100 Women]] for 2016.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-38012048|title=BBC 100 Women 2016: Who is on the list?|date=21 November 2016|newspaper=BBC News|language=en-GB|access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref>  As of 2016, her research interests include [[actin-binding protein]]s in chick embryos and breast cancer, human sperm [[chromatin]] abnormalities, and the effects of [[oxidative stress]] on cell metabolism.<ref name=":0" />

She is an advocate for allowing women to choose their own career path<ref name=":1" /> despite social norms that emphasize marriage and childbearing for women.<ref name=":5" />  She also advocates for legislation supporting women in the workforce such as [[maternity leave]] and childcare provisions.<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last=Sarant|first=Louise|date=7 May 2013|title=Empowering Arab female scientists|url=http://www.natureasia.com/en/nmiddleeast/article/10.1038/nmiddleeast.2013.67|journal=Nature Middle East|doi=10.1038/nmiddleeast.2013.67|access-date=8 December 2016|url-access=subscription}}</ref>  In an interview she said that "Jordan is very permissive when it comes to women's education and work, but traditionally women's priorities are pre-defined: her husband, children and household,"<ref name=":3" /> and noted that 71 of the 80 students in her undergraduate class were women, but only three continued into a master’s program and only one completed a Ph.D.<ref name=":4" />  She also encourages her students, many of whom are women from underprivileged areas of Jordan, to study abroad in order to broaden both their scientific and cultural experiences, with two of her former Master's students doing Ph.D. work in Italy and Canada.<ref name=":2" />

==Awards/Prizes/Orders==

* 2013 Colorado State University Distinguished International Alumni Award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://staff.hu.edu.jo/temp.aspx?pno=16&id=pytjhLqE6Ao=|title=Lubna H. T. TahtamouniAwards/Prizes/Orders|website=staff.hu.edu.jo|access-date=9 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201030553/http://staff.hu.edu.jo/temp.aspx?pno=16&id=pytjhLqE6Ao=|archive-date=1 December 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* College of Natural Sciences Summer International Scholars Program Award, 2012.
* L'OREAL-UNESCO For Women in Science Pan-Arab Regional Fellowship, 2011.
* Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World (OWSD) Award for Young Women Scientists in Biology for the Arab Region for 2011.
* King Hussein Institute for Biotechnology and Cancer (KHIBC) Scholar, 2009.
* First place on the Student Scientific Research Competition, King Abdallah Fund for Development, The Hashemite University, 2008.
*
